stage_results.claim_restriction: Only the existence and reproducibility of an initial Schedule 13D public disclosure clock may be carried forward. No claim that Item 4 language identifies activist/control intent with economically useful precision, causes underreaction, predicts return direction, or survives costs is validated.

primary_findings: SEC guidance effective in the current regime requires an initial Schedule 13D within five business days after acquisition above 5 percent and states the clock runs from trade date.
EDGAR filing detail exposes an acceptance timestamp, so the public-document event clock is reproducible without price or return access.
Initial Schedule 13D can be separated from Schedule 13D/A at the filing-form level.

Item 4 is not a deterministic proxy for control intent: primary filings can contain investment-only/no-control language, reservations of future rights, or evolving intent. A classifier must therefore be frozen ex ante and validated independently before economic testing.
The shortened five-business-day deadline reduces the private accumulation interval versus the former ten-day regime, creating a regime break that must not be silently pooled.
Group formation, derivatives, anticipation and other public information can confound the interpretation of EDGAR acceptance as the first economically informative moment.
active_invalidation: Attempted to invalidate the mechanism by testing whether Schedule 13D itself guarantees control intent. It does not. This invalidates the broad control-intent interpretation but not the narrower documentary disclosure-clock mechanism.
reason_no_handoff: Challenge is not complete with no blocker; BLOCK_CLAIM_LEVEL remains until an ex-ante deterministic Item 4 taxonomy and regime handling are frozen and independently reproducible.
